# Role: Strategist

## Core Mission

As a top-tier AI presentation strategist, receive source documents, perform content analysis and design planning, and output the **Design Specification & Content Outline** (hereafter `design_spec`).

## Pipeline Context

| Previous Step | Current | Next Step |
|--------------|---------|-----------|
| Project creation + Template option confirmed | **Strategist**: Eight Confirmations + Design Spec | Image_Generator or Executor |

> See shared-standards.md for SVG technical constraints, PPT compatibility rules, canvas format table, and post-processing commands.

---

## 1. Eight Confirmations Process

⛔ **BLOCKING**: Before starting analysis, reference `templates/design_spec_reference.md` and provide professional recommendations for the following eight items. If a user is available, present them as a bundled package and wait for confirmation or modifications. If no user is available, apply the recommendations directly and proceed.

> **Execution discipline**: This is the last BLOCKING checkpoint in the pipeline (besides template selection). Once confirmed (or auto-decided in non-interactive mode), the AI must automatically complete the Design Specification & Content Outline and seamlessly proceed to subsequent image generation (if applicable), SVG generation, and post-processing — no additional questions or pauses in between.

### a. Canvas Format Confirmation

Recommend format based on scenario (see canvas format quick reference in shared-standards.md).

### b. Page Count Confirmation

Provide specific page count recommendation based on source document content volume.

### c. Key Information Confirmation

Confirm target audience, usage occasion, and core message; provide initial assessment based on document nature.

### d. Style Objective Confirmation

| Style | Core Focus | Target Audience | One-line Description |
|-------|-----------|----------------|---------------------|
| **A) General Versatile** | Visual impact first | Public / clients / trainees | "Catch the eye at a glance" |
| **B) General Consulting** | Data clarity first | Teams / management | "Let data speak" |
| **C) Top Consulting** | Logical persuasion first | Executives / board | "Lead with conclusions" |

**Style selection decision tree**:

```
Content characteristics?
  ├── Heavy imagery / promotional ──→ A) General Versatile
  ├── Data analysis / progress report ──→ B) General Consulting
  └── Strategic decisions / persuading executives ──→ C) Top Consulting

Audience?
  ├── Public / clients / trainees ────→ A) General Versatile
  ├── Teams / management ────────────→ B) General Consulting
  └── Executives / board / investors → C) Top Consulting
```

### e. Color Scheme Recommendation

Proactively provide a color scheme (HEX values) based on content characteristics and industry.

**Industry color quick reference** (full 14-industry list in `scripts/config.py` under `INDUSTRY_COLORS`):

| Industry | Primary Color | Characteristics |
|----------|--------------|-----------------|
| Finance / Business | `#003366` Navy Blue | Stable, trustworthy |
| Technology / Internet | `#1565C0` Bright Blue | Innovative, energetic |
| Healthcare / Health | `#00796B` Teal Green | Professional, reassuring |
| Government / Public Sector | `#C41E3A` Red | Authoritative, dignified |

**Color rules**: 60-30-10 rule (primary 60%, secondary 30%, accent 10%); text contrast ratio >= 4.5:1; no more than 4 colors per page.

### f. Icon Usage Confirmation

| Option | Approach | Suitable Scenarios |
|--------|----------|-------------------|
| **A** | Emoji | Casual, playful, social media |
| **B** | AI-generated | Custom style needed |
| **C** | Built-in icon library | Professional scenarios (recommended) |
| **D** | Custom icons | Has brand assets |

Built-in library contains 640+ icons; see `templates/icons/README.md`.

> **Mandatory rules when choosing C**:
> 1. Consult `templates/icons/icons_index.json` to verify icon existence
> 2. Icon names are single names (e.g., `factory`), no path prefixes
> 3. Using names not in the index is FORBIDDEN
> 4. List the final icon inventory in the Design Spec; Executor may only use icons from this list
>
> **Quick lookup**: By category → `icons_index.json` `categories`; by semantics → `quickLookup`; full list → `templates/icons/FULL_INDEX.md`

### g. Typography Plan Confirmation (Font + Size)

#### Font Presets

| Scenario | Preset | Title | Body | Emphasis |
|----------|--------|-------|------|----------|
| Modern business, tech | P1 | Microsoft YaHei / Arial | Microsoft YaHei / Calibri | SimHei |
| Government documents, reports | P2 | SimHei | SimSun / Times | SimSun |
| Culture, arts, humanities | P3 | KaiTi / Georgia | Microsoft YaHei | SimHei |
| Traditional, conservative | P4 | SimSun | Microsoft YaHei / Arial | SimSun |
| English-primary | P5 | Arial / Impact | Calibri / Georgia | Arial Black |

#### Font Size Baseline (all sizes in px)

Selection principle: Font size is based on **content density**, not design style.

| Content Density | Points per Page | Body Baseline | Suitable Scenarios |
|----------------|----------------|---------------|-------------------|
| Relaxed | 3-5 items | 24px | Keynote-style, training materials |
| Dense | 6+ items | 18px | Data reports, consulting analysis |

| Level | Ratio | 24px Baseline | 18px Baseline |
|-------|-------|---------------|---------------|
| Cover title | 2.5-3x | 60-72px | 45-54px |
| Page title | 1.5-2x | 36-48px | 27-36px |
| **Body** | **1x** | **24px** | **18px** |
| Annotation | 0.75x | 18px | 14px |

### h. Image Usage Confirmation

| Option | Approach | Suitable Scenarios |
|--------|----------|-------------------|
| **A** | No images | Data reports, process documentation |
| **B** | User-provided | Has existing image assets |
| **C** | AI-generated | Custom illustrations, backgrounds needed |
| **D** | Placeholders | Images to be added later |

**When selection includes B**, you must run `python3 scripts/analyze_images.py <project_path>/images` before outputting the spec, and integrate scan results into the image resource list.

**When B/C/D is selected**, add an image resource list to the spec:

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| Filename | e.g., `cover_bg.png` |
| Dimensions | e.g., `1280x720` |
| Ratio | e.g., `1.78` |
| Layout suggestion | e.g., `Wide landscape (suitable for full-screen/illustration)` |
| Purpose | e.g., `Cover background` |
| Type | Background / Photography / Illustration / Diagram / Decorative pattern |
| Status | Pending generation / Existing / Placeholder |
| Generation description | Fill in detailed description for AI generation |

**Image type descriptions**:

| Type | Suitable Scenarios |
|------|-------------------|
| Background | Full-page backgrounds for covers/chapter pages; reserve text area |
| Photography | Real scenes, people, products, architecture |
| Illustration | Flat design, vector style, concept diagrams |
| Diagram | Flowcharts, architecture diagrams, concept relationship maps |
| Decorative pattern | Partial decoration, textures, borders, divider elements |

**Image-layout alignment principles** (detailed calculation rules in `references/image-layout-spec.md`):

| Image Ratio | Recommended Layout |
|-------------|-------------------|
| > 2.0 (ultra-wide) | Top-bottom split, top full-width |
| 1.5-2.0 (wide) | Top-bottom split |
| 1.2-1.5 (standard landscape) | Left-right split |
| 0.8-1.2 (square) | Left-right split |
| < 0.8 (portrait) | Left-right split, image on left |

Core logic: The layout container's aspect ratio must closely match the image's original ratio. Never force a wide image into a square container or a portrait image into a narrow horizontal strip.

> **Pipeline handoff**: When C) AI generation is selected, after outputting the design spec, prompt the user to invoke Image_Generator. Once images are collected in `images/`, proceed to Executor.

### Chart Reference (Non-blocking — Strategist recommends, no user confirmation needed)

When content outline pages involve **data visualization** (comparisons, trends, proportions, KPIs, flows, strategic frameworks, etc.), consult the chart template library to select appropriate chart types.

Built-in library contains 33 chart templates; see `templates/charts/charts_index.json`.

> **Selection workflow**:
> 1. Identify pages that need data visualization during content planning
> 2. Consult `charts_index.json` — by analysis goal → `quickLookup`; by category → `categories`
> 3. Review `bestFor` / `avoidFor` to confirm the chart type fits the data characteristics
> 4. List all selected charts in Design Spec **section VII (Chart Reference List)** as a centralized reference; in section IX Content Outline, each page only needs to note the chart type name
>
> **Quick lookup by goal**:
> - Ranking/comparison → `bar_chart`, `horizontal_bar_chart`, `grouped_bar_chart`
> - Trends over time → `line_chart`, `area_chart`, `dual_axis_line_chart`
> - Proportions → `donut_chart`, `pie_chart`, `treemap_chart`
> - KPIs/targets → `kpi_cards`, `bullet_chart`, `gauge_chart`
> - Conversion/flow → `funnel_chart`, `sankey_chart`, `waterfall_chart`
> - Strategy → `swot_analysis`, `porter_five_forces`, `matrix_2x2`

### Speaker Notes Requirements (Default — no discussion needed)

- File naming: Recommended to match SVG names (`01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`), also compatible with `notes/slide01.md`
- Fill in the Design Spec: total presentation duration, notes style (formal / conversational / interactive), presentation purpose (inform / persuade / inspire / instruct / report)
- Split note files must NOT contain `#` heading lines (`notes/total.md` master document MUST use `#` heading lines)

---

## 2. Executor Style Details (Reference for Confirmation Item #4)

### A) General Versatile — Executor_General

**Typical scenarios**: Progress reports, financial analysis, government reports, proposals/bids

51	Audience?

53	  ├── Teams / management ────────────→ B) General Consulting
54	  └── Executives / board / investors → C) Top Consulting
55	```

57	### e. Color Scheme Recommendation
58	
59	Proactively provide a color scheme (HEX values) based on content characteristics and industry.
60	
61	**Industry color quick reference** (full 14-industry list in `scripts/config.py` under `INDUSTRY_COLORS`):

63	| Industry | Primary Color | Characteristics |
64	|----------|--------------|-----------------|
65	| Finance / Business | `#003366` Navy Blue | Stable, trustworthy |
66	| Technology / Internet | `#1565C0` Bright Blue | Innovative, energetic |
67	| Healthcare / Health | `#00796B` Teal Green | Professional, reassuring |
68	| Government / Public Sector | `#C41E3A` Red | Authoritative, dignified |
69	
70	**Color rules**: 60-30-10 rule (primary 60%, secondary 30%, accent 10%); text contrast ratio >= 4.5:1; no more than 4 colors per page.
71	
72	### f. Icon Usage Confirmation
73	
74	| Option | Approach | Suitable Scenarios |
75	|--------|----------|-------------------|
76	| **A** | Emoji | Casual, playful, social media |
77	| **B** | AI-generated | Custom style needed |
78	| **C** | Built-in icon library | Professional scenarios (recommended) |
79	| **D** | Custom icons | Has brand assets |
80	
81	Built-in library contains 640+ icons; see `templates/icons/README.md`.
82	
83	> **Mandatory rules when choosing C**:
84	> 1. Consult `templates/icons/icons_index.json` to verify icon existence
85	> 2. Icon names are single names (e.g., `factory`), no path prefixes
86	> 3. Using names not in the index is FORBIDDEN
87	> 4. List the final icon inventory in the Design Spec; Executor may only use icons from this list
88	>
89	> **Quick lookup**: By category → `icons_index.json` `categories`; by semantics → `quickLookup`; full list → `templates/icons/FULL_INDEX.md`
90	
91	### g. Typography Plan Confirmation (Font + Size)
92	
93	#### Font Presets
94	
95	| Scenario | Preset | Title | Body | Emphasis |
96	|----------|--------|-------|------|----------|
97	| Modern business, tech | P1 | Microsoft YaHei / Arial | Microsoft YaHei / Calibri | SimHei |
98	| Government documents, reports | P2 | SimHei | SimSun / Times | SimSun |
99	| Culture, arts, humanities | P3 | KaiTi / Georgia | Microsoft YaHei | SimHei |
100	| Traditional, conservative | P4 | SimSun | Microsoft YaHei / Arial | SimSun |
101	| English-primary | P5 | Arial / Impact | Calibri / Georgia | Arial Black |
102	
103	#### Font Size Baseline (all sizes in px)
104	
105	Selection principle: Font size is based on **content density**, not design style.
106	
107	| Content Density | Points per Page | Body Baseline | Suitable Scenarios |
108	|----------------|----------------|---------------|-------------------|
109	| Relaxed | 3-5 items | 24px | Keynote-style, training materials |
110	| Dense | 6+ items | 18px | Data reports, consulting analysis |
111	
112	| Level | Ratio | 24px Baseline | 18px Baseline |
113	|-------|-------|---------------|---------------|
114	| Cover title | 2.5-3x | 60-72px | 45-54px |
115	| Page title | 1.5-2x | 36-48px | 27-36px |
116	| **Body** | **1x** | **24px** | **18px** |
117	| Annotation | 0.75x | 18px | 14px |
118	
119	### h. Image Usage Confirmation
120	
121	| Option | Approach | Suitable Scenarios |
122	|--------|----------|-------------------|
123	| **A** | No images | Data reports, process documentation |
124	| **B** | User-provided | Has existing image assets |
125	| **C** | AI-generated | Custom illustrations, backgrounds needed |
126	| **D** | Placeholders | Images to be added later |
127	
128	**When selection includes B**, you must run `python3 scripts/analyze_images.py <project_path>/images` before outputting the spec, and integrate scan results into the image resource list.
129	
130	**When B/C/D is selected**, add an image resource list to the spec:
131	
132	| Column | Description |
133	|--------|-------------|
134	| Filename | e.g., `cover_bg.png` |
135	| Dimensions | e.g., `1280x720` |
136	| Ratio | e.g., `1.78` |
137	| Layout suggestion | e.g., `Wide landscape (suitable for full-screen/illustration)` |
138	| Purpose | e.g., `Cover background` |
139	| Type | Background / Photography / Illustration / Diagram / Decorative pattern |
140	| Status | Pending generation / Existing / Placeholder |
141	| Generation description | Fill in detailed description for AI generation |
142	
143	**Image type descriptions**:
144	
145	| Type | Suitable Scenarios |
146	|------|-------------------|
147	| Background | Full-page backgrounds for covers/chapter pages; reserve text area |
148	| Photography | Real scenes, people, products, architecture |
149	| Illustration | Flat design, vector style, concept diagrams |
150	| Diagram | Flowcharts, architecture diagrams, concept relationship maps |
151	| Decorative pattern | Partial decoration, textures, borders, divider elements |
152	
153	**Image-layout alignment principles** (detailed calculation rules in `references/image-layout-spec.md`):
154	
155	| Image Ratio | Recommended Layout |
156	|-------------|-------------------|
157	| > 2.0 (ultra-wide) | Top-bottom split, top full-width |
158	| 1.5-2.0 (wide) | Top-bottom split |
159	| 1.2-1.5 (standard landscape) | Left-right split |
160	| 0.8-1.2 (square) | Left-right split |
161	| < 0.8 (portrait) | Left-right split, image on left |
162	
163	Core logic: The layout container's aspect ratio must closely match the image's original ratio. Never force a wide image into a square container or a portrait image into a narrow horizontal strip.
164	
165	> **Pipeline handoff**: When C) AI generation is selected, after outputting the design spec, prompt the user to invoke Image_Generator. Once images are collected in `images/`, proceed to Executor.

168	
169	When content outline pages involve **data visualization** (comparisons, trends, proportions, KPIs, flows, strategic frameworks, etc.), consult the chart template library to select appropriate chart types.
170	
171	Built-in library contains 33 chart templates; see `templates/charts/charts_index.json`.
172	
173	> **Selection workflow**:
174	> 1. Identify pages that need data visualization during content planning
175	> 2. Consult `charts_index.json` — by analysis goal → `quickLookup`; by category → `categories`
176	> 3. Review `bestFor` / `avoidFor` to confirm the chart type fits the data characteristics
177	> 4. List all selected charts in Design Spec **section VII (Chart Reference List)** as a centralized reference; in section IX Content Outline, each page only needs to note the chart type name
178	>
179	> **Quick lookup by goal**:
180	> - Ranking/comparison → `bar_chart`, `horizontal_bar_chart`, `grouped_bar_chart`
181	> - Trends over time → `line_chart`, `area_chart`, `dual_axis_line_chart`
182	> - Proportions → `donut_chart`, `pie_chart`, `treemap_chart`
183	> - KPIs/targets → `kpi_cards`, `bullet_chart`, `gauge_chart`
184	> - Conversion/flow → `funnel_chart`, `sankey_chart`, `waterfall_chart`
185	> - Strategy → `swot_analysis`, `porter_five_forces`, `matrix_2x2`

187	### Speaker Notes Requirements (Default — no discussion needed)
188	
189	- File naming: Recommended to match SVG names (`01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`), also compatible with `notes/slide01.md`
190	- Fill in the Design Spec: total presentation duration, notes style (formal / conversational / interactive), presentation purpose (inform / persuade / inspire / instruct / report)
191	- Split note files must NOT contain `#` heading lines (`notes/total.md` master document MUST use `#` heading lines)
192	
193	---
194	
195	## 2. Executor Style Details (Reference for Confirmation Item #4)
196	
197	### A) General Versatile — Executor_General
198	
199	**Unique capabilities**:
200	- Full-width images + gradient overlays (essential for promotions)
201	- Free creative layouts (not grid-constrained)
202	- Three style variants: image-text hybrid, minimalist keynote, creative design
203	
204	**Typical scenarios**: Investment promotion, product launches, training materials, brand campaigns
205	
206	**Avoid**: Overly rigid/formal, dense data tables
207	
208	### B) General Consulting — Executor_Consultant
209	
210	**Unique capabilities**:
211	- KPI dashboards (4-card layout, large numbers + trend arrows)
212	- Professional chart combinations (bar, line, pie, funnel)
213	- Data color grading (red/yellow/green status indicators)
214	
215	**Typical scenarios**: Progress reports, financial analysis, government reports, proposals/bids
216	
217	**Avoid**: Flashy decorations, image-dominated slides
218	
219	### C) Top Consulting — Executor_Consultant_Top
220	
221	**Unique capabilities**:
222	
223	| Capability | Description |
224	|-----------|-------------|
225	| Data contextualization | Every data point must have a comparison ("grew 63% — industry average only 12%") |
226	| SCQA framework | Situation → Complication → Question → Answer |
227	| Pyramid principle | Conclusion first; core insight in the title position |
228	| Strategic coloring | Colors serve information, not decoration |
229	| Chart vs Table | Trends → charts; precise values → tables |
230	
231	**Unique page elements**: Gradient top bar + dark takeaway box, confidential marking + rigorous footer, MECE decomposition / driver tree / waterfall chart
232	
233	**Typical scenarios**: Strategic decision reports, deep analysis reports, consulting deliverables (MBB level)
234	
235	**Avoid**: Isolated data, subjective statements, decorative elements
236

239	## 3. Color Knowledge Base
240	
241	### Consulting Style Colors (Professional Authority)
242	
243	| Brand / Style | HEX | Psychological Feel |
244	|---------------|-----|-------------------|
245	| Deloitte Blue | `#0076A8` | Professional, reliable |
246	| McKinsey Blue | `#005587` | Authoritative, deep |
247	| BCG Dark Blue | `#003F6C` | Stable, trustworthy |
248	| PwC Orange | `#D04A02` | Energetic, innovative |
249	| EY Yellow | `#FFE600` | Optimistic, clear |
250	
251	### General Versatile Colors (Modern Energy)
252	
253	| Style | HEX | Suitable Scenarios |
254	|-------|-----|-------------------|
255	| Tech Blue | `#2196F3` | Technology, internet |
256	| Vibrant Orange | `#FF9800` | Marketing, promotion |
257	| Growth Green | `#4CAF50` | Health, environmental, growth |

261	### Data Visualization Colors
262	
263	- Positive trend (green): `#2E7D32` → `#4CAF50` → `#81C784`
264	- Warning trend (yellow): `#F57C00` → `#FFA726` → `#FFD54F`
265	- Negative trend (red): `#C62828` → `#EF5350` → `#E57373`

269	## 4. Layout Pattern Quick Reference
270	
271	| Layout | Suitable Scenarios | PPT 16:9 Reference Dimensions |
272	|--------|-------------------|-------------------------------|
273	| Single column centered | Covers, conclusions, key points | Content width 800-1000px, horizontally centered |
274	| Two-column | Comparative analysis, left-image right-text | Column ratio 1:1 or 3:2, gap 40-60px |
275	| Three-column | Parallel points, process steps | Column ratio 1:1:1, gap 30-40px |
276	| Four-quadrant | Matrix analysis, classification | Quadrant 560x250px, gap 20-30px |
277	| Top-bottom split | Ultra-wide images + text | Image full-width, text area >= 150px height |
278	| Left-right split | Standard/portrait images + text | Image on side, text area >= 280px width |
279	
280	**PPT 16:9 (1280x720) key dimensions**: Safe area 1200x640 (40px margins); Title area 1200x100; Content area 1200x500; Footer area 1200x40.
281	
282	---
283	
284	## 5. Template Flexibility Principle
285	
286	> Templates are starting points, not endpoints.
287	
288	The Strategist should make professional judgments on the template basis generated by `scripts/project_manager.py`, considering user needs, content characteristics, and audience:
289	
290	1. Ratio systems are adjustable (font size ratios are reference values)
291	2. Color schemes are customizable (based on brand and content)
292	3. Layout modes can be combined (6 base layouts with free variation)
293	4. Content structure is extensible (12-chapter framework can be expanded or reduced)
294	5. Spacing / border radius details adjusted by Executor based on content density
295	
296	---
297	
298	## 6. Workflow & Deliverables
299	
300	### 6.1 Content Planning Strategy
301	
302	| Style | Content Outline | Design Spec | Speaker Notes |
303	|-------|----------------|-------------|---------------|
304	| A) General Versatile | Intelligently deconstruct source doc; define core theme per page | Visual theme, color scheme, layout principles | Concise presentation script |
305	| B) General Consulting | Structured logical sections; data-driven insights | Consulting-style colors, structured content layout | Professional terms, data interpretation, conclusion-first |
306	| C) Top Consulting | SCQA framework, pyramid principle conclusion-first | Data contextualization, strategic color usage | Highly condensed, logically rigorous, conclusion-driven |
307	
308	### 6.2 Outline Output Specification (Must include 12 chapters)
309	
310	| Chapter | Content Requirements |
311	|---------|---------------------|
312	| I. Project Information | Project name, canvas format, page count, style, audience, scenario, date |
313	| II. Canvas Specification | Format, dimensions, viewBox, margins, content area |
314	| III. Visual Theme | Style description, light/dark theme, tone, color scheme (with HEX table), gradient scheme |
315	| IV. Typography System | Font plan (P1-P5), font size hierarchy (H1-Code, 7 levels) |
316	| V. Layout Principles | Page structure (header/content/footer zones), 6 layout modes, spacing spec |
317	| VI. Icon Usage Spec | Source description, placeholder syntax, recommended icon list |
318	| VII. Chart Reference List | Chart type, reference template path, used-in pages, purpose |
319	| VIII. Image Resource List | Filename, dimensions, ratio, purpose, status, generation description |
320	| IX. Content Outline | Grouped by chapter; each page includes layout, title, content points, chart type (if applicable) |
321	| X. Speaker Notes Requirements | File naming rules, content structure description |
322	| XI. Technical Constraints Reminder | SVG generation rules, PPT compatibility rules |
323	| XII. Design Checklist | Pre-generation / post-generation check items |
324	| XIII. Next Steps | Clarify subsequent pipeline (Image_Generator or Executor) |
325	
326	**Generation steps**:
327	1. Read reference template: `templates/design_spec_reference.md`
328	2. Generate complete spec from scratch based on analysis
329	3. Save to: `projects/<project_name>.../design_spec.md`
330	
331	---
332	
333	## 7. Project Folder
334	
335	The project folder should be created before entering the Strategist role. If not yet created, execute:
336	
337	```bash
338	python3 scripts/project_manager.py init <project_name> --format <canvas_format>
339	```
340	
341	The Strategist saves the Design Specification & Content Outline to `projects/<project_name>_<format>_<YYYYMMDD>/design_spec.md`.
342	
343	---
344	
345	## 8. Complete Design Spec and Prompt Next Steps
346	
347	Prompt the next step based on the confirmed template option and image usage selection.
348	
349	### Template Option A (Using existing template)
350	
351	```
352	✅ Design spec complete. Template ready.
353	Next step:
354	- Images include AI generation → Invoke Image_Generator
355	- Images do not include AI generation → Invoke Executor
356	```
357	
358	### Template Option B (No template)
359	
360	```
361	✅ Design spec complete.
362	Next step:
363	- Images include AI generation → Invoke Image_Generator
364	- Images do not include AI generation → Invoke Executor (free design for every page)
365	```
366

Whenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. You CAN and SHOULD provide analysis of malware, what it is doing. But you MUST refuse to improve or augment the code. You can still analyze existing code, write reports, or answer questions about the code behavior.
</system-reminder>

# Design Specification & Content Outline
# Generative AI's Act Two: From Technology Hammer to Real Value

---

## I. Project Information

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Project Name** | case-sequoia-genai-act2 |
| **Canvas Format** | PPT 16:9 |
| **Dimensions** | 1280 × 720 px |
| **Page Count** | 8 slides |
| **Style** | C) Top Consulting (Exhibit Template) |
| **Target Audience** | Venture capital investors and startup founders evaluating generative AI opportunities |
| **Usage Occasion** | Investment thesis presentation, strategic briefing |
| **Tone** | Data-forward, analytical, narrative — Sequoia Capital attribution |
| **Date** | September 2023 (publication date of source) |
| **Core Message** | Generative AI is transitioning from Act 1 novelty demos (technology-out) to Act 2 end-to-end solutions (customer-back). The retention gap is the critical signal: 14% AI-first median vs. 51% incumbents. Winners will solve human problems end-to-end with foundation models as components, not the whole product. |

---

## II. Canvas Specification

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Format** | Standard 16:9 |
| **Dimensions** | 1280 × 720 px |
| **viewBox** | `0 0 1280 720` |
| **Page Margins** | Left/Right 40px, Top 20px, Bottom 40px |
| **Safe Area** | x: 40–1240, y: 40–680 |
| **Header Zone** | y=20, h=60px — key message / page title |
| **Content Area** | y=100, h=520px |
| **Footer Zone** | y=660, h=60px — source, confidential label, page number |

---

## III. Visual Theme

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Style** | Top Consulting / Exhibit |
| **Theme Mode** | Dark covers/chapter pages + White content pages |
| **Design Tone** | Premium, refined, authoritative, data-driven, conclusion-first |

### Color Scheme

| Role | HEX | Usage |
|------|-----|-------|
| **Primary Dark** | `#0D1117` | Cover, ending, dark page backgrounds |
| **Content White** | `#FFFFFF` | Content page main background |
| **Gradient Start Blue** | `#1E40AF` | Top gradient bar start |
| **Gradient End Purple** | `#7C3AED` | Top gradient bar end |
| **Gold Accent** | `#D4AF37` | Dividers, left decorations, highlights |
| **Purple-Blue Accent** | `#6366F1` | Chapter numbers, secondary accents |
| **Body Black** | `#111827` | Body text on light backgrounds |
| **Light Gray Text** | `#9CA3AF` | Descriptions, subtitles on dark |
| **Tertiary Text** | `#6B7280` | Footer, timestamps |
| **Card Background Dark** | `#1F2937` | Dark card / key message bar |
| **Divider Light** | `#E5E7EB` | Dividers on light backgrounds |
| **Border Dark** | `#374151` | Borders on dark backgrounds |
| **Data Red** | `#EF4444` | Negative/problem data (AI retention) |
| **Data Green** | `#10B981` | Positive data (incumbent retention) |
| **Data Orange** | `#F59E0B` | Warning/callout |

### Gradient Scheme
- **Top Gradient Bar**: `#1E40AF` → `#7C3AED` (horizontal), height 4–6px, all pages
- **Cover Decorative Gradient**: `#1E40AF` → `#7C3AED` (used on left accent line area)

---

## IV. Typography System

### Font Stack
**Primary**: `Arial, "Helvetica Neue", sans-serif`  
**Mono/Emphasis**: `"Arial Black", Impact, sans-serif`

### Font Size Hierarchy (18px baseline — dense content)

| Level | Usage | Size | Weight | Notes |
|-------|-------|------|--------|-------|
| H1 | Cover main title | 52px | Bold | Letter-spacing 2px |
| H2 | Page main title / Key message bar | 24px | Bold | Letter-spacing 1px |
| H3 | Section title / Chapter large text | 44px | Bold | Semi-transparent BG |
| H4 | Card title / Sub-section header | 18px | Bold | Letter-spacing 1px |
| P | Body content | 14px | Regular | Line-height 1.5 |
| Large Data | Highlighted numbers/KPIs | 42px | Bold | Gold or accent color |
| Sub | Annotations, footer, source | 11px | Regular | `#9CA3AF` |

---

## V. Layout Principles

### Page Structure
| Zone | Y Position | Height | Usage |
|------|-----------|--------|-------|
| Top gradient bar | y=0 | 6px | All pages — blue-purple gradient |
| Key message / header | y=20 | 64px | Dark bar with gold left accent (content pages) |
| Content area | y=100 | 520px | Flexible main content |

**Left Column — Act 1: Technology-Out** (red header `#EF4444`):
- Foundation model = entire product
- Novelty demos / "AI [Incumbent]" wrappers
- Thin wrappers with no workflow integration
- Poor retention and no durable moat
- Technology-first: "What can the model do?"
- Modality-based market organization
- Examples: Undifferentiated copilots, AI Salesforce, AI Adobe

**Right Column — Act 2: Customer-Back** (green header `#10B981`):
- Foundation model = one component of comprehensive solution
- New editing interfaces → stickier workflows
- Multi-modal, end-to-end problem solving
- Durable retention through workflow lock-in
- Customer-first: "What does the user need end-to-end?"
- Use-case-based market organization
- Examples: **Harvey** (legal), **Glean** (enterprise search), **Character** & **Ava** (companions)

Bottom annotation: "The Sequoia market map is now organized by use case, not model modality"
Source: Sequoia Capital, September 2023

---

### Slide 7 — Market Map Reorganized by Use Case
**Layout**: 2×3 use-case grid cards  
**Template**: `03_content.svg`  
**Key Message Bar**: "Market Map Reorganized by Use Case — Not Model Modality"  
**Content**:

Six use-case category cards in 2×3 grid, each with icon + title + exemplar:

| # | Icon | Category | Act 2 Exemplar | Description |
|---|------|----------|----------------|-------------|
| 1 | `shield-check` | Legal | Harvey | Custom LLMs for elite law firms |
| 2 | `magnifying-glass` | Enterprise Search | Glean | Crawling & indexing workspaces for AI |
| 3 | `users` | Companions & Social | Character, Ava | Digital companions — 2hr avg sessions |
| 4 | `sparkles` | Creative & Multimodal | Midjourney | Image gen → $100M+ revenue, 11 people |
| 5 | `rocket` | Developer Tools | ChatGPT (dev) | PMF with developers, fastest-growing app |
| 6 | `layers` | Enterprise Workflows | Glean + category | Multimodal, workflow-integrated solutions |

Bottom statement: "Applications are increasingly multi-modal — the modality lens is obsolete"
Source: Sequoia Capital, September 2023

---

### Slide 8 — Key Takeaways: What Separates Winners in Act Two
**Layout**: Numbered list of 5 takeaways, full-width, dark accent cards  
**Template**: `03_content.svg` (or `04_ending.svg` adapted)  
**Key Message Bar**: "Five Principles for Building and Investing in Act Two"  
**Content**:

Five bold takeaway rows (numbered, icon + headline + brief):

1. **`arrow-trend-down` Retention is the critical signal** — AI-first apps at 14% median vs. 51% for incumbents; a 3.6× gap that exposes lack of real utility
2. **`layers` Foundation models are a component, not the product** — Act 2 winners integrate models into comprehensive, workflow-embedded solutions
3. **`target` Solve human problems end-to-end** — Multi-modal, editing-interface-rich solutions that are stickier and harder to displace
4. **`dollar` $1B+ revenue proves real demand exists** — GenAI startups hit this faster than SaaS; the opportunity is real despite the hype cycle
5. **`trophy` Use case beats modality** — The new market map is organized around human problems: legal, search, companionship, creative, developer, enterprise

Bottom attribution: "Source: Sonya Huang, Pat Grady and GPT-4 — Sequoia Capital, September 2023"
Footer: CONFIDENTIAL | Sequoia Capital Analysis

---

## X. Speaker Notes Requirements

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **File naming** | `notes/total.md` (master), split to `notes/slide_01.md` … `notes/slide_08.md` |
| **Total duration** | ~20 minutes (2.5 min/slide average) |
| **Notes style** | Formal, data-driven, persuasive |
| **Presentation purpose** | Persuade — inform investors and founders of the Act 1→Act 2 shift and actionable implications |

Notes structure per slide: (1) Opening hook, (2) Key data point to cite, (3) Transition to next slide.  
Split note files must NOT contain `#` heading lines (reserved for total.md master document).

---

## XI. Technical Constraints Reminder

- viewBox: `0 0 1280 720` on every SVG
- Use `<rect>` for all backgrounds
- Text wrapping via `<tspan>` only — no `<foreignObject>`
- Transparency via `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` — no `rgba()`
- Prohibited: `clipPath`, `mask`, `<style>`, `class`, `foreignObject`, `textPath`, `animate*`, `script`, `marker`/`marker-end`
- Arrows: `<polygon>` triangles only
- Gradients: `<defs>` + `<linearGradient>`
- No `<g opacity="...">` — set opacity on each child element individually
- Inline styles only — no external CSS or `@font-face`
- Icon placeholders: `[[icon:icon-name]]` syntax — embedded by `finalize_svg.py`

---

## XII. Design Checklist

**Pre-generation**:
- [x] Canvas format confirmed (1280×720, ppt169)
- [x] Eight Confirmations complete
- [x] Color scheme locked (exhibit dark theme)
- [x] Typography plan locked (Arial/Calibri, 18px baseline)
- [x] Icon inventory verified against icons_index.json
- [x] Chart types selected and verified against charts_index.json
- [x] All data sourced exclusively from source_brief.md — no fabrication

**Post-generation**:
- [ ] All SVGs saved to `svg_output/`
- [ ] Speaker notes saved to `notes/total.md`
- [ ] `total_md_split.py` executed
- [ ] `finalize_svg.py` executed (icon embed, text flatten)
- [ ] `svg_to_pptx.py` executed with `-s final`

---

## XIII. Next Steps

No AI image generation required (Option A — no images).

**→ Proceed directly to Executor Phase (Top Consulting style)**

Read:
- `references/executor-base.md`
- `references/executor-consultant-top.md`

Then generate 8 SVG pages sequentially into `svg_output/`.

# Executor Common Guidelines

> Style-specific content is in the corresponding `executor-{style}.md`. Technical constraints are in shared-standards.md.

---

## 1. Template Adherence Rules

If template files exist in the project's `templates/` directory, the template structure must be followed:

| Page Type | Corresponding Template | Adherence Rules |
|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|
| Cover | `01_cover.svg` | Inherit background, decorative elements, layout structure; replace placeholder content |
| Chapter | `02_chapter.svg` | Inherit numbering style, title position, decorative elements |
| Content | `03_content.svg` | Inherit header/footer styles; **content area may be freely laid out** |
| Ending | `04_ending.svg` | Inherit background, thank-you message position, contact info layout |
| TOC | `02_toc.svg` | **Optional**: Inherit TOC title, list styles |

### Page-Template Mapping Declaration (Required Output)

Before generating each page, you must explicitly output which template (or "free design") is used:

```
📝 **Template mapping**: `templates/01_cover.svg` (or "None (free design)")
🎯 **Adherence rules / layout strategy**: [specific description]
```

- **Content pages**: Templates only define header and footer; the content area is freely laid out by the Executor
- **No template**: Generate entirely per the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 2. Design Parameter Confirmation (Mandatory Step)

> Before generating the first SVG page, you **must review the key design parameters from the Design Specification & Content Outline** to ensure all subsequent generation strictly follows the spec.

Must output confirmation including: canvas dimensions, body font size, color scheme (primary/secondary/accent HEX values), font plan.

**Why is this step mandatory?** Prevents the "spec says one thing, execution does another" disconnect.

---

## 3. Execution Guidelines

- **Proximity principle**: Place related elements close together to form visual groups; increase spacing between unrelated groups to reinforce logical structure
- **Absolute spec adherence**: Strictly follow the color, layout, canvas format, and typography parameters in the spec
- **Follow template structure**: If templates exist, inherit the template's visual framework
- **Phased batch generation** (recommended):
  1. **Visual Construction Phase**: Generate all SVG pages continuously, ensuring high consistency in design style and layout coordinates (Visual Consistency)
  2. **Logic Construction Phase**: After all SVGs are finalized, batch-generate speaker notes to ensure narrative coherence (Narrative Continuity)
- **Technical specifications**: See [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md) for SVG technical constraints and PPT compatibility rules

### SVG File Naming Convention

File naming format: `<number>_<page_name>.svg`

- **Chinese content** → Chinese naming: `01_封面.svg`, `02_目录.svg`, `03_核心优势.svg`
- **English content** → English naming: `01_cover.svg`, `02_agenda.svg`, `03_key_benefits.svg`
- **Number rules**: Two-digit numbers, starting from 01
- **Page name**: Concise and descriptive, matching the page title in the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 4. Icon Usage

Four approaches: **A: Emoji** (`<text>🚀</text>`) | **B: AI-generated** (SVG basic shapes) | **C: Built-in library** (`templates/icons/` 640+ icons, recommended) | **D: Custom** (user-specified)

**Built-in icons — Placeholder method (recommended)**:

```xml
<use data-icon="chart-bar" x="100" y="200" width="48" height="48" fill="#005587"/>
```

> No need to manually run `embed_icons.py`; `finalize_svg.py` post-processing tool will auto-embed icons.

**Common icons**: `chart-bar` `arrow-trend-up` `users` `cog` `circle-checkmark` `target` `clock` `file` `dollar` `lightbulb`

114	## 7. Font Usage
115	
116	Apply corresponding fonts for different text roles based on the font plan in the Design Specification & Content Outline:
117	
118	| Role | Chinese Recommended | English Recommended |
119	|------|--------------------|--------------------|
120	| Title font | Microsoft YaHei / KaiTi / SimHei | Arial / Georgia |
121	| Body font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Calibri / Times |
122	| Emphasis font | SimHei | Arial Black / Consolas |
123	| Annotation font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Arial / Times |
124	
125	---
126	
127	## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework
128	
129	### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document
130	
131	After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.
132	
133	**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.
134	
135	**Format**: Each page starts with `# <number>_<page_title>`, separated by `---` between pages. Each page includes: script text (2-5 sentences), `Key points: ① ② ③`, `Duration: X minutes`. Except for the first page, each page's text starts with a `[Transition]` phrase.
136	
137	**Basic stage direction markers** (common to all styles):
138	
139	| Marker | Purpose |
140	|--------|---------|
141	| `[Pause]` | Whitespace after key content, letting the audience absorb |
142	| `[Transition]` | Standalone paragraph at the start of each page's text, bridging from the previous page |
143	
144	> Each style may extend with additional markers (`[Interactive]`/`[Data]`/`[Scan Room]`/`[Benchmark]` etc.), see `executor-{style}.md`.
145	
146	**Requirements**:
147	
148	- Notes should be conversational and flow naturally
149	- Highlight each page's core information and presentation key points
150	- Users can manually edit and override in the `notes/` directory
151	
152	### Task 2. Split Into Per-Page Note Files
153	
154	Automatically split `notes/total.md` into individual speaker note files in the `notes/` directory.
155	
156	**File naming convention**:
157	
158	- **Recommended**: Match SVG names (e.g., `01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`)
159	- **Compatible**: Also supports `slide01.md` format (backward compatibility)
160	
161	---
162	
163	## 9. Next Steps After Completion
164	
165	> **Auto-continuation**: After Visual Construction Phase (all SVG pages) and Logic Construction Phase (all notes) are complete, the Executor proceeds directly to the post-processing pipeline.
166	
167	**Post-processing & Export** (see [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md)):

171	python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>
172	
173	# 2. SVG post-processing (auto-embed icons, images, etc.)
174	python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>
175	
176	# 3. Export PPTX
177	python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
178	# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
179	```

27

40

44	| **Benchmark** | "X vs industry average Y" | Bar chart with gray dashed baseline |
45	| **Competitive comparison** | "Us X vs Competitor Y" | Side-by-side bar chart, highlight own data |
46	| **Target gap** | "Actual X / Target Y" | Progress bar + gap annotation |
47	| **Ranking** | "Ranked #N of M" | Horizontal bar chart + highlight marker |
48

71	```
72	
73	| Level | Position | Font Size |
74	|-------|----------|-----------|
75	| Core conclusion | Takeaway Box | 16-18px bold |
76	| Arguments | Content area body | 14-16px |
77	| Supporting data | Charts / cards | 12-14px |
78

96	│ Content area (x=40, y=140,       │  ← Charts / data / analysis
97	│   w=1200, h=520)                 │
98	├──────────────────────────────────┤
99	│ Source | CONFIDENTIAL | Page #    │  ← y=700, 10px
100	└──────────────────────────────────┘
101	```
102	
103	### Strategic Roadmap
104	
105	Three phases laid out horizontally, `<rect rx="8">` + title + action list, `<polygon>` arrows connecting:
106	
107	```
108	Focus Core (0-6mo)  ──>  Expand Capability (6-12mo)  ──>  Scale Up (12-18mo)
109	x=40,w=380              x=450,w=380                     x=860,w=380
110	```
111

113	
114	Horizontal table; own row highlighted in theme color, others in gray. Leading indicators marked green, lagging marked red. Use `<circle>` or `<rect>` to build score points.
115

117	
118	Start → increase/decrease factors → End. Positive factors green bars, negative factors red bars, start/end points dark bars, cumulative line as dashed connector.
119

121	
122	## Strategic Use of Color
123	
124	MBB-level color usage is extremely restrained — color serves information:
125	
126	| Purpose | Method |
127	|---------|--------|

178	
179	[Transition] Having clarified the problem and the opportunity, now comes the most critical part — our response path.
180	
181	We recommend a three-phase strategy. [Pause]

193	Flex: [If time is tight, skip phase two and three details and go straight to financial impact]
194	```

211	- [ ] **Visual hierarchy**: Conclusion > Arguments > Details, differentiated by font size/weight
212	- [ ] **Brand consistency**: Gradient top bar and footer unified throughout

217	- [ ] **Stage markers complete**: [Pause] and [Scan Room] at key positions

# Executor Consultant Top — Top-tier Consulting Style (MBB Level)

> Common guidelines: executor-base.md. Technical constraints: shared-standards.md.

---

## Role Definition

An MBB-level (McKinsey / Bain / BCG) top-tier consulting style SVG design executor. Suitable for strategic planning, board presentations, investment roadshows, C-suite decision support, and other **premium consulting** scenarios. Core characteristics: data-driven insights, pyramid-structured narrative, extreme simplicity. Output targets C-level decision-makers.

---

## SCQA Framework (Narrative Structure)

Every MBB-level presentation follows the SCQA narrative structure:

| Element | Purpose | Typical Pages |
|---------|---------|---------------|
| **S - Situation** | Establish shared context | Cover / Pages 1-2 |
| **C - Complication** | Introduce the problem / tension | Pages 2-3 |
| **Q - Question** | The implicit or explicit question to solve | Transition page |
| **A - Answer** | Core solution | All body pages |

**Page sequencing**: Cover embodies S+C → Executive Summary answers Q → Chapters develop A → Closing revisits S

**Title writing**:

| SCQA Element | Weak Title | MBB-level Title |
|-------------|------------|-----------------|
| S | "Industry Background" | "Digital penetration surpasses 60%, industry enters deep waters" |
| C | "Challenges Faced" | "Yet three structural contradictions constrain scaled deployment" |
| Q | "Strategic Question" | "How to move from pilot to full deployment within 18 months?" |
| A | "Solution" | "Three-phase path: Focus, Expand, Scale" |

---

## Data Contextualization (Never Present Data in Isolation)

> **Golden Rule**: Never display a single data point in isolation. Every number needs context.

| Method | Pattern | Visual Implementation |
|--------|---------|----------------------|
| **Time comparison** | "From X to Y" | Line chart + arrow annotating magnitude of change |
| **Benchmark** | "X vs industry average Y" | Bar chart with gray dashed baseline |
| **Competitive comparison** | "Us X vs Competitor Y" | Side-by-side bar chart, highlight own data |
| **Target gap** | "Actual X / Target Y" | Progress bar + gap annotation |
| **Ranking** | "Ranked #N of M" | Horizontal bar chart + highlight marker |

**Data annotation three essentials**: Every data visualization must include (1) The value itself (large bold font) (2) Comparison reference (baseline / prior period / competitor) (3) Meaning interpretation ("So what?")

```xml

1	# Executor Consultant Top — Top-tier Consulting Style (MBB Level)
2	
3	> Common guidelines: executor-base.md. Technical constraints: shared-standards.md.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Role Definition
8	
9	An MBB-level (McKinsey / Bain / BCG) top-tier consulting style SVG design executor. Suitable for strategic planning, board presentations, investment roadshows, C-suite decision support, and other **premium consulting** scenarios. Core characteristics: data-driven insights, pyramid-structured narrative, extreme simplicity. Output targets C-level decision-makers.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## SCQA Framework (Narrative Structure)
14	
15	Every MBB-level presentation follows the SCQA narrative structure:
16	
17	| Element | Purpose | Typical Pages |
18	|---------|---------|---------------|
19	| **S - Situation** | Establish shared context | Cover / Pages 1-2 |
20	| **C - Complication** | Introduce the problem / tension | Pages 2-3 |
21	| **Q - Question** | The implicit or explicit question to solve | Transition page |
22	| **A - Answer** | Core solution | All body pages |
23	
24	**Page sequencing**: Cover embodies S+C → Executive Summary answers Q → Chapters develop A → Closing revisits S
25	
26	**Title writing**:
27	
28	| SCQA Element | Weak Title | MBB-level Title |
29	|-------------|------------|-----------------|
30	| S | "Industry Background" | "Digital penetration surpasses 60%, industry enters deep waters" |
31	| C | "Challenges Faced" | "Yet three structural contradictions constrain scaled deployment" |
32	| Q | "Strategic Question" | "How to move from pilot to full deployment within 18 months?" |
33	| A | "Solution" | "Three-phase path: Focus, Expand, Scale" |
34	
35	---
36	
37	## Data Contextualization (Never Present Data in Isolation)
38	
39	> **Golden Rule**: Never display a single data point in isolation. Every number needs context.
40	
41	| Method | Pattern | Visual Implementation |
42	|--------|---------|----------------------|
43	| **Time comparison** | "From X to Y" | Line chart + arrow annotating magnitude of change |
44	| **Benchmark** | "X vs industry average Y" | Bar chart with gray dashed baseline |
45	| **Competitive comparison** | "Us X vs Competitor Y" | Side-by-side bar chart, highlight own data |
46	| **Target gap** | "Actual X / Target Y" | Progress bar + gap annotation |
47	| **Ranking** | "Ranked #N of M" | Horizontal bar chart + highlight marker |
48	
49	**Data annotation three essentials**: Every data visualization must include (1) The value itself (large bold font) (2) Comparison reference (baseline / prior period / competitor) (3) Meaning interpretation ("So what?")
50	
51	```xml
52	<text x="160" y="280" text-anchor="middle" font-size="42" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">97.3%</text>
53	<text x="160" y="310" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Industry avg 82% | Competitor A 89%</text>
54	<text x="160" y="335" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#059669">Leading industry by 15.3 percentage points</text>
55	```
56	
57	---
58	
59	## Pyramid Principle (Conclusion First)
60	
61	> Executives don't care about your *process* — they care about *results*.
62	
63	```
64	         ┌─────────────────┐
65	         │  Core Conclusion │   ← Page title / Takeaway
66	         └────────┬────────┘
67	      ┌───────────┼───────────┐
68	  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐
69	  │ Arg 1 │  │ Arg 2 │  │ Arg 3 │   ← Key supporting points
70	  └───────┘  └───────┘  └───────┘
71	```
72	
73	| Level | Position | Font Size |
74	|-------|----------|-----------|
75	| Core conclusion | Takeaway Box | 16-18px bold |
76	| Arguments | Content area body | 14-16px |
77	| Supporting data | Charts / cards | 12-14px |
78	
79	**Contrast**: Title "Market Research Results" (wrong) → "Metaverse needs 5-10 years to reach scale" (right); Body "We researched... and found..." (wrong) → "Three arguments: (1)... (2)... (3)..." (right)
80	
81	---
82	
83	## MBB-level Layout Patterns
84	
85	### Content Page Standard Structure (1280x720)
86	
87	```
88	┌──────────────────────────────────┐
89	│ Gradient top bar (0,0 → 1280,6)  │
90	├──────────────────────────────────┤
91	│ Assertion title (x=40, y=50, 24px)│
92	├──────────────────────────────────┤
93	│ Takeaway Box (x=40, y=75,        │  ← Dark background + white text, one-sentence conclusion
94	│   w=1200, h=45)                  │
95	├──────────────────────────────────┤
96	│ Content area (x=40, y=140,       │  ← Charts / data / analysis
97	│   w=1200, h=520)                 │
98	├──────────────────────────────────┤
99	│ Source | CONFIDENTIAL | Page #    │  ← y=700, 10px
100	└──────────────────────────────────┘
101	```
102	
103	### Strategic Roadmap
104	
105	Three phases laid out horizontally, `<rect rx="8">` + title + action list, `<polygon>` arrows connecting:
106	
107	```
108	Focus Core (0-6mo)  ──>  Expand Capability (6-12mo)  ──>  Scale Up (12-18mo)
109	x=40,w=380              x=450,w=380                     x=860,w=380
110	```
111	
112	### Benchmarking Matrix
113	
114	Horizontal table; own row highlighted in theme color, others in gray. Leading indicators marked green, lagging marked red. Use `<circle>` or `<rect>` to build score points.
115	
116	### Waterfall Chart (Change Attribution)
117	
118	Start → increase/decrease factors → End. Positive factors green bars, negative factors red bars, start/end points dark bars, cumulative line as dashed connector.
119	
120	---
121	
122	## Strategic Use of Color
123	
124	MBB-level color usage is extremely restrained — color serves information:
125	
126	| Purpose | Method |
127	|---------|--------|
128	| **Focus** | Target data in theme color, everything else gray |
129	| **Reduce cognitive load** | Same series differentiated by opacity (`fill-opacity` 1.0/0.6/0.3) |
130	| **Semantics** | Green = positive, Red = negative, Gray = baseline |
131	| **Branding** | Gradient top bar / decorative lines in brand color |
132	
133	**Commandments**: No more than 3 primary colors; accent color used at most 2-3 places globally; data series use same-hue depth variations, not different colors; background white or very light gray.
134	
135	---
136	
137	## Chart vs Table Selection Matrix
138	
139	| Scenario | Recommended Form | Reason |
140	|----------|-----------------|--------|
141	| Comparing 2-7 categories | **Bar chart** | Visual comparison is intuitive |
142	| Time trends | **Line chart** | Time series clarity |
143	| Precise values / large rankings | **Table** | 50 data points in a bar chart would be chaotic |
144	| Proportional composition | **Donut chart** | More modern than pie charts |
145	| Two-dimensional positioning | **2x2 matrix** | Strategic quadrant analysis |
146	| Change attribution | **Waterfall chart** | Factor decomposition |
147	
148	---
149	
150	## Speaker Notes Style
151	
152	### Narrative Tone
153	
154	Targeting **executives / decision-makers**. Pyramid structure — every sentence carries information. Composed, authoritative, and insightful tone.
155	
156	### Stage Direction Markers
157	
158	| Marker | Purpose | Example |
159	|--------|---------|---------|
160	| `[Pause]` | Silence after key insight, let executives absorb | "This means we are missing a billion-dollar market. [Pause]" |
161	| `[Scan Room]` | Observe decision-makers' reactions, decide whether to elaborate | "[Scan Room] If there are questions, I can elaborate." |
162	| `[Data]` | Conversational number delivery | "[Data] 63% → nearly two-thirds" |
163	| `[Benchmark]` | Emphasize comparison baseline | "[Benchmark] Compared to the industry average of 12%, our 23% is nearly double" |
164	| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Building on the strategic framework, let's drill into the implementation path." |
165	
166	### Notes Writing Guidelines
167	
168	- **Pyramid structure**: Conclusion → Arguments → Details
169	- **Data contextualization**: Every number has a comparison reference
170	- **Executive language**: "The strategic implication is...", "The core insight is..."
171	- **Flex mechanism**: Annotate "content that can be skipped if time is tight" for flexible duration
172	- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core insight (2) Data support (3) Strategic implication`
173	
174	### Notes Example
175	
176	```markdown
177	# 03_strategic_path
178	
179	[Transition] Having clarified the problem and the opportunity, now comes the most critical part — our response path.
180	
181	We recommend a three-phase strategy. [Pause]
182	
183	Phase one: Focus. Over the next six months, concentrate resources on conquering the Eastern China market.
184	[Data] Eastern China contributes nearly two-thirds of industry growth, [Benchmark] yet our penetration rate is only half of Competitor A's. [Pause]
185	
186	Phase two: Expand. Use Eastern China as a template, replicate to Southern and Northern China.
187	Phase three: Scale. Leverage a digital platform for nationwide coverage.
188	
189	[Scan Room] The resource allocation for phase one is in the appendix — would you like me to walk through it now?
190	
191	Key points: (1) Focus-Expand-Scale three-phase approach (2) Data-backed Eastern China priority (3) 18-month full deployment
192	Duration: 3 minutes
193	Flex: [If time is tight, skip phase two and three details and go straight to financial impact]
194	```
195	
196	---
197	
198	## MBB-level Quality Checklist Supplement
199	
200	### Content Level
201	
202	- [ ] **SCQA complete**: Overall follows Situation-Complication-Question-Answer structure
203	- [ ] **Data contextualized**: Every data point has a comparison reference
204	- [ ] **Conclusion first**: Every page's Takeaway Box has a one-sentence conclusion
205	- [ ] **MECE principle**: Categorized analysis is mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive
206	
207	### Visual Level
208	
209	- [ ] **Color with intent**: Colors serve information delivery
210	- [ ] **Ample whitespace**: Not crowded; information can "breathe"
211	- [ ] **Visual hierarchy**: Conclusion > Arguments > Details, differentiated by font size/weight
212	- [ ] **Brand consistency**: Gradient top bar and footer unified throughout
213	
214	### Notes Level
215	
216	- [ ] **Pyramid structure**: Every page is conclusion-first
217	- [ ] **Stage markers complete**: [Pause] and [Scan Room] at key positions
218	- [ ] **Flex content annotated**: Supports flexible duration

  <defs>

    </linearGradient>
    <linearGradient id="bar1-grad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#1E40AF" stop-opacity="0.9"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#3B82F6" stop-opacity="0.7"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <linearGradient id="bar2-grad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#4F46E5" stop-opacity="0.9"/>

    </linearGradient>
    <linearGradient id="bar3-grad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#7C3AED" stop-opacity="0.9"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#A855F7" stop-opacity="0.7"/>
    </linearGradient>
  </defs>
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="4" fill="url(#top-grad)"/>

  <!-- Takeaway / Key message bar -->
  <rect x="40" y="12" width="1200" height="56" fill="#0D1117"/>
  <rect x="40" y="12" width="6" height="56" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <text x="60" y="47" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" letter-spacing="0.5">Six Decades of Technological Progress Converged to Enable Generative AI</text>

  <!-- Section label -->
  <text x="60" y="100" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" letter-spacing="1">TECHNOLOGICAL FOUNDATIONS</text>

  <!-- === Wave 1: Moore's Law — 6 Decades === -->
  <!-- Bar -->
  <rect x="60" y="118" width="860" height="110" fill="url(#bar1-grad)" rx="6"/>
  <!-- Icon placeholder -->
  <use data-icon="microchip" x="82" y="138" width="40" height="40" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
  <!-- Label -->
  <text x="140" y="152" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold">6 Decades of Moore's Law</text>
  <text x="140" y="175" fill="#BFDBFE" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13">Compute: delivered exaflops of processing power to train and run foundation models</text>
  <!-- Duration badge -->
  <rect x="770" y="130" width="130" height="36" fill="#D4AF37" rx="4"/>
  <text x="835" y="153" text-anchor="middle" fill="#0D1117" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">1960 → Today</text>

  <!-- === Wave 2: Internet — 4 Decades === -->
  <rect x="60" y="246" width="700" height="110" fill="url(#bar2-grad)" rx="6"/>
  <use data-icon="globe" x="82" y="266" width="40" height="40" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
  <text x="140" y="280" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold">4 Decades of the Internet</text>
  <text x="140" y="303" fill="#DDD6FE" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13">Data: produced trillions of tokens of training data (accelerated by COVID)</text>
  <rect x="610" y="258" width="130" height="36" fill="#D4AF37" rx="4"/>
  <text x="675" y="281" text-anchor="middle" fill="#0D1117" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">1983 → Today</text>

  <!-- === Wave 3: Mobile + Cloud — 2 Decades === -->
  <rect x="60" y="374" width="540" height="110" fill="url(#bar3-grad)" rx="6"/>
  <use data-icon="mobile" x="82" y="394" width="40" height="40" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
  <text x="140" y="408" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold">2 Decades of Mobile & Cloud</text>
  <text x="140" y="431" fill="#E9D5FF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13">Distribution: a supercomputer in every human's palm</text>
  <rect x="450" y="386" width="130" height="36" fill="#D4AF37" rx="4"/>
  <text x="515" y="409" text-anchor="middle" fill="#0D1117" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">2003 → Today</text>

  <!-- Convergence arrow -->
  <polygon points="940,220 980,220 980,230 1000,205 980,180 980,190 940,190" fill="#D4AF37" fill-opacity="0.9"/>

  <!-- GenAI result node -->
  <rect x="1010" y="160" width="210" height="140" fill="#0D1117" rx="10"/>
  <rect x="1010" y="160" width="210" height="4" fill="url(#top-grad)" rx="2"/>
  <text x="1115" y="210" text-anchor="middle" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" letter-spacing="1">GENERATIVE AI</text>
  <text x="1115" y="234" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11">Foundation Models</text>
  <text x="1115" y="252" text-anchor="middle" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10">ChatGPT launch 2022</text>
  <text x="1115" y="272" text-anchor="middle" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10">"Cambrian explosion"</text>

  <!-- Spark annotation -->
  <text x="60" y="510" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-style="italic">"ChatGPT's launch was the spark that ignited a Cambrian explosion of innovation not seen since the early internet."</text>
  <text x="60" y="530" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11">— Sonya Huang, Pat Grady & GPT-4, Sequoia Capital</text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <line x1="40" y1="648" x2="1240" y2="648" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="40" y="678" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10">Source: Sequoia Capital, September 2023</text>
  <text x="640" y="678" text-anchor="middle" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10">CONFIDENTIAL</text>
  <text x="1220" y="678" text-anchor="end" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12">2</text>
</svg>

arguments.content:
# 01_cover

[Transition] Welcome. Today we're presenting Sequoia Capital's analysis of generative AI's next act.

The title says it all: we're moving from "Technology Hammer" to "Real Value." This isn't about whether generative AI is real — it is. It's about whether the companies building on it are creating durable value, or just demos. [Pause]

This analysis was published by Sonya Huang, Pat Grady, and GPT-4 at Sequoia Capital in September 2023.

Key points: (1) The deck tells a two-act story about generative AI's maturation (2) Act 1 was about the technology; Act 2 is about the customer (3) Data-driven — retention and revenue benchmarks drive every conclusion
Duration: 1 minute

---

# 02_convergence

[Transition] To understand where generative AI is going, we need to understand what enabled it — and it didn't happen overnight.

Three converging waves made this possible. Six decades of Moore's Law gave us the compute. Four decades of the internet — accelerated by COVID — gave us trillions of tokens of training data. Two decades of mobile and cloud gave us distribution: a supercomputer in every human's palm. [Pause]

[Data] These weren't three separate inventions — they were three layers of infrastructure stacking on top of each other, each enabling the next. ChatGPT's launch was simply the match that lit the fuse.

Key points: (1) Generative AI is 60 years of infrastructure converging (2) No single wave was sufficient — all three were required (3) This explains why it happened now, not 5 years earlier
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 03_revenue_traction

[Transition] So when the spark was lit, how fast did it catch?

Faster than anything we've seen before. Generative AI startups crossed $1 billion in revenue — from startups alone — faster than SaaS ever did. [Benchmark] SaaS took years to reach this milestone; generative AI did it in months. [Pause]

Three standout performers illustrate the range: ChatGPT became the fastest-growing application in history. Midjourney reported hundreds of millions in revenue with just 11 employees. Character.ai achieved 2-hour average sessions — users aren't just trying it, they're living in it.

[Scan Room] Here's the critical caveat: these successes don't change the reality that many AI companies lack product-market fit or sustainable competitive advantage. The headline number is real. But it's hiding a problem.

Key points: (1) $1B+ faster than SaaS — commercial proof point is real (2) Three very different success vectors: productivity, creative, companionship (3) Aggregate revenue masks individual company retention crisis
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 04_retention_gap

[Transition] The problem — and this is the core tension of the whole analysis — shows up in retention data.

[Data] Look at the left panel. Incumbent consumer apps — WhatsApp, Instagram, YouTube — retain between 30% and 85% of their Day-30 users. The median is 51%. These are hard numbers built over years of product refinement.

Now look at the right panel. AI-first apps — Character.ai, Runway, ChatGPT, Lensa — cluster between 12% and 41%. The median is 14%. [Pause]

[Benchmark] That's a 3.6 times gap. Incumbents retain users at 3.6 times the rate of AI-first apps. This is not a rounding error — this is a structural problem.

The one exception is Character.ai at 41% — approaching incumbent levels. [Scan Room] That tells us something important: companionship and entertainment may be generative AI's strongest consumer use case, because the emotional hook drives genuine return behavior.

Key points: (1) 14% AI-first median vs. 51% incumbent median — 3.6× structural gap (2) Poor retention signals lack of genuine utility, not just novelty wear-off (3) Character.ai at 41% is the outlier — companionship drives return behavior
Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 05_monthly_active_usage

[Transition] If Day-30 retention wasn't alarming enough, monthly active usage data shows the full height of the bar AI must clear.

Incumbents aren't just retaining users — they're deeply embedded in daily life. YouTube at 85% monthly active usage. Instagram at 73%. Even Candy Crush at 48%. The median across these nine apps is 63%. [Pause]

[Benchmark] Against that benchmark, the AI-first median of 14% Day-30 retention looks even more stark. The gap isn't 3.6× — when you add monthly engagement, it's even wider.

This is the bar. Not 14%. Not 51%. Sixty-three percent monthly active usage is what it looks like when a consumer app truly works. Act 2 companies need a plan to get there.

Key points: (1) Incumbent median MAU of 63% — the real competitive benchmark (2) AI apps must close a 49+ percentage point engagement gap (3) This is the empirical target for Act 2 builders
Duration: 2 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, this slide can be summarized in 60 seconds — just cite the 63% median and move to Act 1 vs. Act 2]

---

# 06_act1_vs_act2

[Transition] So what explains the retention gap? Sequoia's answer is structural: Act 1 companies were built technology-out. Act 2 companies are being built customer-back.

The left column describes Act 1. The foundation model was treated as the entire product. Every pitch was "AI [Incumbent]" — AI Salesforce, AI Adobe. These were thin wrappers with no workflow integration, no editing interface, no reason to come back. [Pause]

The right column describes what Act 2 looks like. The foundation model is just one component. The product wraps it in a new editing interface, integrates it into an existing workflow, and solves the problem end-to-end. The question isn't "what can the model do?" — it's "what does the user need, start to finish?"

[Data] The exemplars are instructive: Harvey builds custom LLMs for elite law firms — the whole legal workflow. Glean crawls and indexes enterprise workspaces. Character and Ava build digital companions. Each one owns a use case, not just a model call.

And crucially — the Sequoia market map is now organized by use case, not model modality. That reorganization isn't cosmetic. It reflects the shift in how value is actually being created.

Key points: (1) Act 1: tech-out, thin wrappers, poor retention (2) Act 2: customer-back, end-to-end, workflow-integrated (3) Harvey, Glean, Character, Ava as concrete Act 2 exemplars
Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 07_market_map

[Transition] What does this look like in practice? The market is reorganizing around use cases — six of which we see emerging with real traction.

Legal with Harvey. Enterprise search with Glean. Companions and social with Character and Ava. Creative and visual with Midjourney. Developer tools with ChatGPT. And the broader enterprise workflow category that crosses all modalities. [Pause]

What's striking is how different these are from each other — and how multi-modal they're becoming. Harvey isn't just a text model. Midjourney isn't just image generation. The applications that are winning are mixing modalities because human problems require mixed solutions.

[Benchmark] The old market map was organized by what the model could do — text, image, code. The new one is organized by what the customer needs — legal work done, enterprise search, a companion, creative output. That's the shift.

Key points: (1) Six use-case categories emerging with real traction (2) Multi-modal nature of winning applications (Harvey, Glean, Character, Ava, Midjourney) (3) The reorganization signals Act 1 → Act 2 transition is underway
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 08_takeaways

[Transition] So what should builders and investors take away from this analysis?

Five principles. First: retention is the signal. Fourteen percent median is a crisis, not a feature. If users aren't coming back, the product doesn't work. [Pause]

Second: foundation models are components, not products. The companies winning — Harvey, Glean, Character, Ava — are building around the model. The model is a layer, not the ceiling.

Third: solve human problems end-to-end. Multi-modal, workflow-integrated, with editing interfaces that create lock-in. Not point solutions — complete solutions.

[Data] Fourth: the $1 billion-plus in startup revenue is real. The demand exists. This isn't a hype cycle with no underlying reality. Midjourney built a hundred-million-dollar business with 11 people. The opportunity is as large as it appears.

Fifth — and this is the strategic implication for investors — use case beats modality. The winners of Act 2 will be defined by which human problems they own, not which models they use. Map your portfolio and pipeline accordingly.

[Scan Room] The question for every builder in this room: is your company Act 1 or Act 2?

Key points: (1) Retention is the critical diagnostic signal — 14% vs. 51% (2) Foundation models as components enable durable, workflow-integrated solutions (3) $1B+ revenue proves demand; use-case focus determines who captures it
Duration: 3 minutes
